description:
Redwood Inference will publish a public-facing benchmark report focused on production economics: latency per dollar (and supporting throughput/cost metrics) broken down by model family and cloud region. The project combines a rigorous, reproducible measurement effort (methodology, data QA, and internal validation) with a coordinated go-to-market launch across web/docs, press/analysts, lifecycle marketing, sales enablement, and partner channels.

Goals:
- Establish Redwood as the credible reference for “production economics” benchmarking (latency/$) across popular open models and regions.
- Drive qualified inbound (PLG + sales-assisted) for Hosted API and Dedicated/Private by pairing the report with clear CTAs and follow-up motions.
- Arm Sales/SE/CS with consistent talk tracks, competitive framing, and a defensible methodology FAQ.

Scope (what’s included):
- Benchmark definition: workloads (chat + embeddings baseline), concurrency/sequence length distributions, and measurement windows.
- Coverage: a curated set of models (top demand + strategic) and Redwood regions (NA/EU + at least one APAC region), reported per region.
- Outputs: a web landing page + downloadable report PDF, data tables (internal), charts, methodology appendix, and a “how to reproduce” internal guide.
- Launch assets: blog/docs updates, social/email copy, press/analyst briefing pack, partner co-marketing kit, and sales enablement materials (deck, one-pager, objection handling, FAQ).

Out of scope:
- Publishing raw per-request logs or customer-identifying traces.
- Claiming absolute superiority without confidence intervals/controls; results will emphasize methodology and constraints.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Marketing: Camila Reyes (exec sponsor), Ben Carter (campaign owner).
- Applied ML / Performance & Evals: Jonas Weber (methodology sponsor), Claire Dubois + Rina Kobayashi (benchmark execution and data validation).
- Sales/Solutions: Jordan Blake + Stephanie Nguyen + Lukas Meyer (field alignment), Markus Klein (SE readiness and technical talk track).
- Customer Success/Support: Jasmine Liu + Dev Patel (support readiness, inbound handling, escalation paths).

High-level timeline (typical 6–8 weeks):
1) Kickoff + scope lock (models/regions/workloads, success metrics, launch date).
2) Benchmark execution + QA (repeat runs, variance analysis, anomaly triage).
3) Report drafting + internal review (methodology, claims, charts, legal/brand checks).
4) Asset production (landing page, PDF, enablement deck, email/social, partner kit).
5) Launch week (coordinated announcements, press/analyst briefings, sales training).
6) Post-launch analysis (traffic, conversions, pipeline influence, follow-up experiments).

Constraints and risks:
- Reproducibility/credibility: methodology must be explicit; avoid cherry-picking and ensure region-to-region comparability.
- Operational load: benchmark runs must not impact production SLOs; capacity windows and guardrails required.
- Messaging consistency: align Marketing claims with Sales talk track and Support guidance to prevent confusion during inbound surge.

files.description: Published internal methodology: workloads, prompts/input distributions, concurrency settings, warmup/caching policy, how latency/$ is computed, and guidance on interpreting results.
Definition of which model families and cloud regions are included, inclusion criteria, and planned refresh cadence.
How to handle surprising results: variance thresholds, rerun rules, suspected infra noise vs runtime changes, and who signs off.
Rules for external performance claims: acceptable comparisons, confidence intervals/variance language, disclaimers, and review/approval checklist.
Messaging doc: positioning, key narratives, headline stats, approved language, do/don’t list, and how to explain latency/$ to engineers and procurement.
Competitive enablement: anticipated competitor pushback, how Redwood differentiates, and rebuttals tied to methodology.
Field deck structure for AEs/SEs: storyline, slides list, demo flow, and appendices (methodology, region table, pricing tie-in).
FAQ for security-minded prospects: what data is used, no customer data disclosure, retention, and how benchmarks avoid exposing sensitive telemetry.
Support/CS readiness: expected inbound categories, macros/response templates, escalation paths, and SLA expectations during launch week.
Draft release note entry tying any minor product/docs updates needed for the report (e.g., new region availability notes, dashboard screenshots, docs clarifications).
Operational runbook for running benchmark-lab: environment setup, capacity scheduling, required config, output formats, and sanity checks.
Capacity plan for benchmark execution across regions (reserved windows, safety limits, monitoring, and rollback criteria if production risk appears).
Working outline of the report: section headers, chart inventory, narrative notes, and open questions for reviewers.
Early draft copy (rough, iterative): intro, methodology summary, findings, and call-to-action variants; includes inline reviewer comments.
Chart specification doc: exact plots to generate, axes/units, color rules, and mapping from raw metrics to visuals.
Landing page wirecopy: hero message, explainer sections, FAQ, CTAs, and SEO keyword targets.
Launch checklist spreadsheet-style doc: tasks, owners, due dates, dependencies (web, docs, email, PR, partners, enablement, support readiness).

Social copy pack (LinkedIn/X): multiple angles, short/long variants, model/region spotlights, and UTM plan.
Press release draft plus boilerplate, quotes placeholders (CRO/VP Marketing/VP Applied ML), and embargo plan.

Partner kit: summary, approved blurbs, co-branded slide placeholders, and coordination checklist for marketplaces/integration partners.
Working notes from Sales/SE: expected objections (variance, region differences, workload mismatch) and draft responses.
Plan for measuring launch impact: web traffic, report downloads, signup conversions, sales meetings booked, pipeline influence, and cohort definitions.
Internal ‘sheet-like’ export of benchmark runs (by model/region/config): p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, and derived latency/$.
QA notes: outliers, reruns, infra noise investigation, and final sign-off checklist from Perf/Evals.
